checklist.why: "How a state is said"; points to Row/Button for a status that acts
Dot, word, line, tokens, separator named and shown
The Word variant is used by no atlas screen; real state chips are filled badges from TaskRow, farrowing and health tags
States declared none (text only) with reasons; default and live shown
Every tone carries a word; colour never alone
No length cap for a status word; no long or zh example
Live region mounted empty and filled; port notes given
Raw 4px separator margin; no CSS-variable list
No classification line; no table of related look-alikes (Row chip, health tag)
All tones and lines render at 375px without overflow

variants.name: Word (dot + word)
findings: No screen renders it; every live status chip is a filled badge instead

variants.name: Line (coloured values)
findings: The look-alikes are hand-built (TaskDay .tk-tone "late", farrowing "Overdue · 3 days" row text), not statusLine()

variants.name: Chip (filled, as built in screens), undocumented
findings: Three implementations: TaskRow .tk-chip (To do / Done / Late) and farrowing .state-word / .done-word (Active / Done)
"To do" is green on green-wash, but green means done/recorded; the README forbids filled badges

findings.text: Status is not what the product uses. Every state chip in the atlas is a filled badge built outside it: TaskRow .tk-chip (To do / Done / Late on piglet-processing.pen-list) and farrowing .state-word / .done-word (Active / Done on farrowing.room). The README says "never a filled badge".
findings.fix: Decide one face. Either add a "chip" variant to Status (filled wash, 10px/600, 20px tall) and have TaskRow and farrowing call SentriUI.status({ variant: "chip" }), or move those screens to the dot-word. Do not keep both.

findings.text: "To do" is drawn green (rgb 39,102,64 on green-wash) on the pen list, so pens not yet done wear the "done" colour, while "Done" is grey.
findings.fix: Map To do to muted (or amber when due now), Done to green, Late to amber, through Status tones rather than per-feature CSS.

findings.text: Health tags (Thin, Fever, Arthritis) do a different job: they name a recorded condition with a care level, not a workflow state. They are .recorded-tag pills with their own amber/orange tones.
findings.fix: Keep them out of Status; give them their own component (ConditionTag) with care-level tones, and link it from Status's Related list.

findings.text: Status-line look-alikes are hand-built: TaskDay's mono "late" (.tk-tone) and farrowing's "Overdue · 3 days" row text.
findings.fix: Render them with SentriUI.statusLine([...], { mono: true }) so the tone rule (colour on the value, word in ink) holds.

findings.text: "Due tomorrow" on farrowing rows is a forecast in muted 14/500 with no dot. It is fine as text, but the README does not say a forecast is not a Status.
findings.fix: Add one line: forecasts ("Due tomorrow", "Expected in 5 days") are row text, not a Status word.

findings.text: No word-length cap or zh example; raw 4px separator margin.
findings.fix: Cap the word length, add a zh example, and tokenise the separator margin.

proposals.name: Status · chip (filled)
proposals.why: The filled state chip is the de-facto Status on four screens, with three implementations

proposals.name: ConditionTag (health tag)
proposals.why: Thin / Fever / Arthritis label a recorded condition with a care level, a different job from a workflow state
